notes:
Batch T (cough/cold and nasal products). Five of six medicines are no-uk-product: (1) paracetamol/pseudoephedrine/chlorphenamine and (2) the same with caffeine: emc and the MHRA products index (SPC search by each ingredient and by the clinic trade name) list paracetamol+pseudoephedrine, chlorphenamine+pseudoephedrine and paracetamol+pseudoephedrine+diphenhydramine products, but no UK product with paracetamol+pseudoephedrine+chlorphenamine (with or without caffeine). (3) dextromethorphan/guaifenesin: no UK combination; the MHRA 2009 cough-and-cold DSU states such combinations were being phased out (quote: 'Some combinations (such as cough suppressants and expectorants) are being phased out'). (4) bromhexine: no UK SmPC/PIL on emc or MHRA products (MHRA search only returned acetylcysteine documents). (5) sodium chloride 0.9% nasal drops: no UK licensed medicine found (the only 0.9% sodium chloride SmPCs found are eye drops, nebuliser and injection products); saline nasal drops may be sold as medical devices, which have no SmPC, but this was NOT confirmed from a UK source. Because SCHEMA forbids rules on no-uk-product medicines, the MHRA 2009 advice that cough and cold medicines containing pseudoephedrine, chlorphenamine, dextromethorphan or guaifenesin should not be used in children under 6 years could not be attached to those entries as rules; it is attached to xylometazoline (paediatric section). Group memberships added: sympathomimetic for xylometazoline (its own SmPCs) and for the four pseudoephedrine-containing master medicines (pseudoephedrine SmPC 5.1 quote; loratadine-pseudoephedrine and cetirizine-pseudoephedrine are other batches' medicines, added so the xylometazoline contraindication with other sympathomimetic decongestants fires - remove if their own batch defines it differently); serotonergic for dextromethorphan/guaifenesin (dextromethorphan SmPC 5.1 quote, so sertraline/tramadol serotonergic rules fire); antihistamine for the two chlorphenamine combinations (MHRA 2009 DSU). Source conflicts for xylometazoline 0.1% spray: maximum duration 7 days in the 0.1% spray SmPC revised Feb 2024 (emc; same text re-uploaded on MHRA products Aug 2026, so still current for that product) vs 5 days in the SmPC revised 14/10/2026 and the MHRA DSU of April 2026 (both kept; MHRA says product information is being updated). The 2024 SmPC lists narrow-angle glaucoma, rhinitis sicca, phaeochromocytoma and prostatic hypertrophy in 4.3 and says use with MAOIs/tri- and tetracyclic antidepressants may raise blood pressure; the 2026 SmPC does not list these and says interactions via other routes are unlikely. The 0.05% child drops SmPC (different UK product, not the clinic form) is stricter (contraindicates beta-blockers, hypertension/cardiovascular disease, diabetes, hyperthyroidism); recorded as detail items only, no rules. Condition 'phaeochromocytoma' is new and overlaps batch N's 'phaeochromocytoma-untreated'; integrator may wish to merge. Mirtazapine was not added to the tricyclic group (no UK source found calling it tetracyclic). BNF/BNFC not accessed (geo-blocked). AUDIT 2026-10-17 (second checker): no-uk-product status confirmed for all five with the MHRA products search index (no SPC/PIL with dextromethorphan+guaifenesin, bromhexine, paracetamol+pseudoephedrine+chlorphenamine with or without caffeine, or a sodium chloride nasal product); clinic link emc 11927 for dextromethorphan/guaifenesin is a dextromethorphan-only product. Group memberships for the no-uk-product combinations are kept: each rests on a UK source for the ingredient (pseudoephedrine SmPC 5.1, MHRA 2009 DSU list, dextromethorphan SmPC 5.1). See audit/T-U.md.
CROSS-BATCH GROUP AUDIT 2026-10-17 (audit/groups-cross-batch.md): new group 'decongestant' (xylometazoline + the four pseudoephedrine products, quotes in XB.json); xylometazoline:interaction:sympathomimetic now targets it. 'sympathomimetic' is the broad group (adds the beta-2 agonist inhalers). Conditions 'phaeochromocytoma-untreated' -> 'phaeochromocytoma' linked in tool.json conditionImplies.
